title: Gluing Local Contexts into Global Meaning: A Sheaf-Theoretic Decomposition of Transformer Representations
claim: Paired representations are projected into a shared space whose disagreement operator splits into a stable content subspace and a context-dependent remainder.
layout: Single panel, left-to-right, two inputs merge then split into two outputs, math labels on arrows
description: A single left-to-right diagram. Two blue cylinders on the left, labeled h_a and h_b in R^d, each send a curved dark arrow labeled P^T to a central red cylinder labeled R^k, the edge stalk. Beneath it is the coboundary formula (δ^0 h)_e = P^T(h_b − h_a). From the red cylinder two arrows fan out to the right. A blue arrow goes to a blue slab labeled H^0 = ker L_F. A red arrow goes to a red slab, which stands for the H^1 directions. The Laplacian formula L_F = (δ^0)^T δ^0 sits between the two arrows. Color carries the meaning: blue is stable content and red is context-dependent variation. The eye goes first to the central red cylinder and then to the split into blue and red outputs.
caption: Sheaf decomposition of a paraphrase pair. Hidden states ha, hb pass through P ⊤into the edge stalk Rk, where the coboundary measures their disagreement, (δ0h)e = P ⊤(hb −ha). The bottom and top eigenspaces of the sheaf Laplacian LF split the edge stalk Rk into H0 (blue, content stable across phrasing) and the H1 directions (red, context-dependent variation).
abstract: Prior research into interpretability does not test whether a representation stays consistent under paraphrasing. Each pair of paraphrases can be thought of as a local witness that two activations should be the same. From these local witnesses we can build a cellular sheaf on the paraphrase graph. The question of what is consistent under paraphrasing can be answered by the Laplacian $L_\mathcal{F}$ given a frozen model. No training required. Our kernel $H^0$ gives us a content subspace. We show that with only 20 dims the kernel outperforms the subspace that LEACE retains with all dims on held-out CounterFact fact retrieval by $+17.1$\,pp on average across 8 models. By constraining all paraphrases of a fact together we see an additional increase of $+6.5$\,pp. Our spectral complement shows us where the causal influence is concentrated. Ablating the coordinates that vary the most when paraphrased (which approximates ablating the spectral complement at the coordinate level) leads to $5.6$ to $26.5\times$ larger changes in model outputs compared to ablating coordinates with matched per-coordinate variability. We find this across 9 models from 124M to 13B params. By stacking layers we can create a grid which has $b_1 = N(L-1)$ algebraic 1-cycles. The harmonic mass derived from the model varies by nearly 3 orders of magnitude between the 6 architectures. It also tracks the order of steering fragility (Spearman's $Ï= 0.90$, exact one-sided permutation $p = 0.014$). The kernel, its spectral complement and the harmonic mass all come from the same paraphrase graph. Project page: https://cwru-aism.github.io/gluing-lc-page/.
